name: ml-competition-ai-rules-census
made_by: MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents working in his name
method: For each platform or contest the platform-wide terms page (or, where none exists, the standard per-competition rules template) was fetched on 2026-10-17 and searched for: AI-assisted or AI-generated code; AutoML; commercial LLM APIs inside a solution; external data; pre-trained models; whether companies or legal entities may enter; age and sanctions; winner code terms; reproducibility audits. Quotes are verbatim fragments of at most 125 characters each. 'read_how' says whether the primary page was read directly, read from a saved copy, or only seen through search-result snippets.
headline: Of 9 platforms or contests whose primary terms were read, 0 have any clause on AI-assisted or AI-generated code. The rules that actually bind an AI-made entry are indirect: natural-person-only eligibility (DrivenData, Kaggle), open-source / no-paid-service rules that forbid commercial LLM APIs inside a solution (Zindi, bitgrit), and reproducibility audits (NeurIPS EEG/EMG 2026, bitgrit, Zindi).

platforms.name: Zindi
platforms.automl_clause: Automated machine learning tools such as AutoML are not permitted.
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: forbidden indirectly: 'You may only use tools available to everyone i.e. no paid services or free trials that require a credit card.' and 'The solution must use publicly-available, open-source packages only.'
platforms.external_data: Unless stated, no external data sets are allowed in Zindi competitions.
platforms.pretrained_models: You may use pretrained models as long as they are openly available to everyone.
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: not addressed; framed as individuals or teams of up to four; 'Prizes are transferred only to individual players or to the team leader.'
platforms.winner_code_terms: Top 3 in prized competitions assign copyright in the winning solution code to Zindi unless competition rules say otherwise; proof of ID, residence and a bank letter required.
platforms.reproducibility: Code requested from top 10 within 48 h; 'If your code does not run you will be dropped from the top 20.' 'Always set the seed.'

platforms.name: AIcrowd
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: not addressed platform-wide; per-challenge rules take precedence: 'the order of precedence shall be as follow: (i) the Challenge Rules; (ii) these Participation Terms; (iii) the ToU.'
platforms.external_data: not addressed platform-wide; third-party materials must be disclosed at submission
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: not restricted: 'Any User having opened an Account as Participant will have the right to participate to the Challenges'
platforms.winner_code_terms: Entrant chooses the licence; if none is stated 'the MIT open source license (https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) will apply to all software code'. Challenge rules may require extra rights for a reward.

platforms.name: DrivenData
platforms.scope: standard per-competition rules template (no site-wide terms page found)
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: not addressed; the non-exclusive-licence variant refers to components that 'depend on or are produced by proprietary systems or commercial products (the "Proprietary Elements")'
platforms.external_data: varies by competition; this one: 'External data is permitted in this Competition provided Participants have all rights, licenses and permissions'
platforms.pretrained_models: this competition: participants 'may use external data other than the Data, including pre-trained models'
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: NO: 'Legal entities and organizations are not eligible for entry.' Open 'to all natural persons who are a legal resident of a country, state, province or territory within the Territory'
platforms.age_or_sanctions: 'at least eighteen years of age and the age of majority in their jurisdiction of residence'; 'not the target of any trade sanctions administered or enforced by the United States'; people 'located in the Russian Federation are not eligible to win a prize in this Competition.'
platforms.winner_code_terms: 'Winning solutions need to be made available under the MIT License' 'in order to be eligible for recognition and prize money if offered.'
platforms.reproducibility: winning model documentation template; 'Privately sharing code or data outside of teams is not permitted.'

platforms.name: Kaggle
platforms.scope: Foundational Competition Rules (appended to every competition's /rules page) plus the common AMLT clause
platforms.read_how: search snippets only; the rules page is JS-rendered and returned only its title to a plain fetch
platforms.automl_clause: per competition, commonly: 'This competition permits the use of automated machine learning tool(s) ("AMLT") in the creation of Submissions.' (snippet)
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: not addressed as such; external tools must be 'reasonably accessible to all' and of 'minimal cost' (snippet, Gemini Long Context rules)
platforms.external_data: template: 'The use of external data and models is acceptable unless specifically prohibited by the Host.' (snippet)
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: NO in practice: 'Each Team member must be a single individual with a separate Kaggle account.' (snippet)
platforms.age_or_sanctions: residents of Crimea, DNR, LNR, Cuba, Iran, Syria, North Korea or persons under U.S. sanctions may not enter (snippet)
platforms.reproducibility: per competition; code competitions run inside Kaggle Notebooks
platforms.note: Kaggle also requires a live-selfie identity check before submitting to many competitions (observed by MV2's biotech field on 2026-10-14).

platforms.name: Codabench
platforms.scope: platform-wide (Privacy Policy and Terms of Use, effective 2023-03-28)
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: not addressed; each competition's organiser-supplied terms govern
platforms.age_or_sanctions: none stated; 'In case of dispute, the French law will apply.'
platforms.winner_code_terms: 'The contents provided in Codabench is the property of the competition organizers' 'unless otherwise stated in the competition's terms of use.'

platforms.name: NeurIPS 2026 EEG/EMG Foundation Challenge (hosted on Codabench)
platforms.external_data: 'Pre-train on any public dataset. Declare all of it.' 'The sealed test split is never allowed, and closed clinical datasets are not allowed.'
platforms.pretrained_models: 'pre-training on any publicly available, redistributable dataset is allowed.' 'Original dataset and model licenses remain in force.'
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: YES: 'Industry, academia, students, and independents are all eligible, and cross-institution teams are encouraged.' 'Anyone can enter. Organisers cannot win prizes.'
platforms.winner_code_terms: 'Participants retain the intellectual property rights they hold in their submitted code, models, and related materials.' 'Open-source release after the competition is encouraged, but remains entirely the participant's choice.'
platforms.reproducibility: 'The top three per track must replay within ±2σ.' 'we re-run your training pipeline from the committed config and re-score the resulting weights against the sealed split.'

platforms.name: Wunder Fund Alfa Connectome (limit-order-book contest)
platforms.read_how: saved verbatim copy made by MV2's hands on 2026-10-16, re-read 2026-10-17
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: not addressed; the scoring sandbox has no network, so none could run
platforms.external_data: 'No external data: Your solution must only use the training data we provide.'
platforms.pretrained_models: 'Pre-trained models are allowed: You may use open-source pre-trained models, provided they are publicly available and do not contain external market data.'
platforms.winner_code_terms: prizes require code, a 2-8 page report and a 30-60 minute code-review video call
platforms.reproducibility: 'Please don't share your code, models, or detailed strategies publicly before the competition is over.' 'Private sharing between participants is also not allowed.'

platforms.name: ThinkOnward
platforms.scope: platform-wide Onward Challenge Terms and Conditions (as shown on the Patch the Planet challenge)
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: not addressed; Section 13 bars code under 'the GNU GPL or LPGL or any similar "copyleft" license'
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: YES: 'if you are agreeing to these Challenge Terms on behalf of a company, an organization, or other legal entity' then 'the term "you" or "Participant" means Your Organization on whose behalf you are acting'
platforms.age_or_sanctions: 'the older of (i) 18 years of age; and (ii) the age of majority in the Participant's relevant jurisdiction of residency'; 'open to residents of the United States and other countries worldwide, except for Restricted Parties'; restricted jurisdictions listed as 'Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, the Crimea Region of Ukraine (including Sevastopol)' plus occupied areas of four Ukrainian regions
platforms.winner_code_terms: winners grant a 'worldwide, non-exclusive, sub-licensable, transferable, fully paid-up, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable license' 'for any purpose whatsoever, for commercial uses or otherwise, without your further approval or further payment to you'
platforms.reproducibility: winners sign documents and give one interview of up to an hour

platforms.name: bitgrit (AI Immune System Challenge)
platforms.scope: contest rules (bitgrit publishes rules per competition)
platforms.commercial_llm_api_inside_solution: FORBIDDEN: 'The use of commercial or proprietary APIs (e.g., OpenAI GPT series, Claude, Gemini API) is strictly prohibited'
platforms.external_data: 'The use of external datasets (e.g., additional training samples or labels from other sources) is strictly prohibited.'
platforms.pretrained_models: 'The use of publicly available, open-source pre-trained models (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa, Llama, etc.) and Embedding models is' permitted
platforms.legal_entities_may_enter: individuals only: 'All submissions must be made by individuals; team submissions are not allowed.'
platforms.winner_code_terms: README with 'Clear, unambiguous instructions to reproduce the predictions from start to finish'; weights or a permanent link to the exact pre-trained model version
platforms.reproducibility: 'Participants must fix all random seeds and set the inference temperature to 0 (where applicable)'

not_covered.name: Solafune
not_covered.reason: https://solafune.com/about/terms returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-17; rules are per competition

not_covered.name: Numerai
not_covered.reason: https://docs.numer.ai/numerai-tournament/rules returned HTTP 404; the Terms of Service at https://numer.ai/terms were not read this run

not_covered.name: CrunchDAO
not_covered.reason: rules sit behind sign-up; an earlier reading (MV2 playbook) found KYC and one account per natural person

not_covered.name: Signate
not_covered.reason: no platform-wide AI clause found by search in Japanese or English; the terms page was not read

not_covered.name: Tianchi
not_covered.reason: only search snippets: one 2025 challenge said 'commercial LLM API calls is prohibited'; the platform terms were not read

prior_art_checked.what: mlcontests.com State of Competitive ML 2023 and State of ML Competitions 2024
prior_art_checked.finding: report how winners used LLMs and note one competition that required specific open-weight models; no rules census

prior_art_checked.what: Nasios, 'The ecosystem of machine learning competitions', arXiv:2604.08001 (2026-04-09)
prior_art_checked.finding: no analysis of AI-tool rules; the terms ChatGPT, AI-assisted and AI agents do not appear

prior_art_checked.what: 'Ethical guidelines for machine learning competitions', AI and Ethics (Springer, 2026), doi 10.1007/s43681-026-01201-4
prior_art_checked.finding: compares Kaggle, AIcrowd and DrivenData rules; paywalled, so whether it tabulates AI-assistance clauses could not be checked. Limit of this census.
compares code evaluation, private evaluation and similar features; no AI-use policy column

limits: Nine primary texts, one date. Rules change; per-competition rules can override every platform-wide term quoted here.
Kaggle quotes come from search-result snippets of rules pages, not from a direct read; Kaggle's pages are JS-rendered.
Quotes are fragments of at most 125 characters, so some sentences are split; the URL gives the full text.
Absence of a clause is reported as 'not addressed', never as 'allowed'.
